abstract: This paper introduces a method to increase capacitive coupling between transmitter antenna and receiver antenna using coil shape design and a method to reduce the traditional 2 pairs capacitive coupling to 1 pair coupling by using different equipotential zone to allow current circulation in receiver circuit. The performance of the proposed methods had shown better capacitive coupling than using sheet plate and constant coupling in distance misalignment.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Optimization of The MCR-WPT System with Uncertain Parameters
abstract: Uncertainty in the environment brings great challenges to maintaining high performance for the magnetically-coupled resonant wireless power transfer (MCR- WPT) system. For example, in the underwater MCR-WPT system, uncertain changes in water temperature, salinity, or water velocity may cause changes in the system parameters and decrease the power transmission efficiency drastically. In order to improve the system performance, the uncertain parameters in the MCR-WPT system is analyzed first, and then an interval-based uncertain optimization method is proposed to find the optimal values of the compensation networks in the MCR-WPT system. Numerical simulations are carried out to verify the proposed uncertain optimization method. The results demonstrate that, using the proposed method, the MCR-WPT system can achieve high average power transfer efficiency or good robustness performance when the uncertain parameters vary within certain ranges.

articleTitle: Possibility of the Undersea Wireless Power Transfer Using a Cone Spiral Coil
abstract: In this study, the shape of receiving coil for undersea wireless power transfer via coupled magnetic resonance was studied. A simulation model based on the actual measurement environment was created, and transmission efficiencies using two shapes of coils were compared. The simulation results show that the power transfer efficiency of the cone spiral coil in the sea is 81.5%, which is useful for undersea wireless power transfer in the deep sea. To protect an electronics device from the high pressure in the deep sea, the electronics devices are contained in a spherical glass housing. If the receiving coil is formed along the spherical surface of the glass housing, the inside of the housing can be used more widely. This is the advantage of the cone spiral coil.

Author Keywords: Coupled Magnetic Resonance Deep Sea Exploration

articleTitle: The Suppression of Far-Field Radiation from Two-Dimensional Structures Larger than a Wavelength
abstract: In this paper, a condition is found on the geometry of two-dimensional, spatially-periodic, oscillating current density patterns such that far-field radiation is suppressed. Suppression becomes better for larger structures, even when the dimensions of the structure exceed the free-space wavelength. For the specific case of a metamaterial array consisting of a square grid of resonators with alternating current directions, far-field radiation will be suppressed as long as the nearest diagonal center-to-center distance between resonators is less than the free-space wavelength.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of the Coupling Factor for Single and Multi-layered Circular, Square, and Hexagonal Wireless Power Transfer Coils
abstract: This paper proposes a method to compute the coupling factor of single and multi-layered coils having a square, hexagonal, or circular geometry, placed center to center to each other, such that there is no lateral or angular misalignment, and only vertical misalignments are of interest. Existing methods involve using 2D / 3D electromagnetic solvers, elliptical integrals, Bessel function, magnetic vector potential, or a combination of these methods. All these methods increase computational complexity and are not in a compact form. The calculation of the coupling factor requires the computation of mutual inductance and the self-inductance of the coils. The self-inductance of single-layered coils is calculated using Modified Wheeler's eq. and the self-inductance for multi-layered coils is calculated using a combination of Modified Wheeler's eq. (for the inductance of each layer) and elliptical integrals (for mutual inductance between layers). The mutual inductance of single and multi-layered coils is derived based on the series expansion of Neumann's eq. with an addition of a factor to reduce the maximum error from 37% to 6.64%. A side length transformation eq. is derived and proposed for equivalent coil transformation from a hexagonal coil to a circular coil or vice versa. The method proposed here requires only geometric quantities of the coils for the computation of mutual inductance. Simulation and experimental results showed excellent agreement with the proposed model of separation distances greater than the inner radius of the transmitter (Tx) or receiver (Rx) coil (whichever has a smaller inner radius). For simulation results, an error of up to 5% was seen for single-layered coils and an error of up to 6.64% was seen for multi-layered coils. For experimental results, the error was under 5% for double-layered air coils and 8.1% for single-layered coils with a ferrite core at separation distances greater than the inner radius of the coils. Hence, the coupling factor can be computed accurately with the proposed model at separation distances greater than the inner radius of Tx or Rx coil.

articleTitle: Harvesting for Scattering Bluetooth-Signals between Battery-less Transponder and Mobile Telephones
abstract: This work studies harvesting of electromagnetic energy from intentionally generated wireless signals (RF signal) as a power supply for a battery-less transponder in the 2.4 GHz ISM Band. The transponder (back-)scatters the incident RF signal by reflecting and modulating such that it is receivable by a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) receiver of a mobile telephone. This scattering includes signal modulation with a 4 MHz frequency shift of the incident signal and frequency shift keying for information transmission. Modulation is controlled by a low energy micro-controller, which receives its operational energy from a RF harvesting circuit that accumulates energy from the incident RF signal. In contrast to our previously used continuous wave transmitter, the present work studies the feasibility of using the BLE transmitter of a further mobile telephone for providing the incident RF signal. This approach requires dealing with the intermittent nature of practical wireless communication, which motivates us to use features of the BLE Standard version 5.0, namely the extended advertizing messages and their periodic re- transmissions. Our experiments involve a specifically designed code sequence, which generates a quasi-continuous wave signal of approx. 2 ms duration, which provides the basis for the transponder's scattering process. Thus, by using energy and waveform of a RF signal from a transmitting mobile telephone we achieved wireless communication from a battery-less transponder to a separate receiving mobile telephone, which encourages further endeavors in this direction.

articleTitle: Optimal Annular Structures for Resonant Magnetic Wireless Power Receivers
abstract: Previous studies of flat, multi-turn spiral resonators have found that the effective series resistance may be reduced by splitting the conducting traces. [1] [2] In this paper, the special case of two-dimensional, single-turn, multi-annulus resonators with rotational symmetry is studied. Optimal inter-annulus gaps and annulus widths are found for resonators consisting of a fixed number of annuli and a fixed outer diameter. In addition, an optimal distribution of capacitance is found for bridging a radial gap in a wide annulus.

articleTitle: Percutaneous Wireless Powering System for a Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) with an Internal Backup Battery
abstract: This study deals with the analysis of an optimum configuration for a wireless powering system applied to a left ventricular assisted device (LVAD). The current models of LVAD are miniaturized pump that are attached directly to heart by mini-invasive technique and can be used to treat advanced heart pathologies. The pump is electrically driven by a DC brushless motor powered by an external battery connected to the motor by percutaneous driveline cable. This last is cause of many infections and should be eliminated. Aim of this work is the study of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system used to power the motor replacing the percutaneous driveline. Electrical performances, safety aspects and reliability of the system are all aspects of paramount importance. A backup battery integrated with the implanted secondary coil is also proposed. This solution permits to improve the system reliability with a minimum number of components that must be subcutaneously implanted.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Broadband RF-to-DC Rectifier on Short Pulses
abstract: In this work, the performance of a recently proposed broadband RF-to-DC rectifier is evaluated for short pulses. The rectifier is designed to cover 0.61 - 1.36 GHz based on the impedance bandwidth. However, this impedance bandwidth is based on the measurement at discrete frequencies and may not be linearly scalable to short wideband pulses due to the nonlinear characteristics of the diodes. Therefore, in order to evaluate the performance of the rectifier on short pulses, a test is performed via circuit simulation using Gaussian input pulses with various pulsewidths and pulse repetition intervals. The results demonstrate that the broadband rectifier still exhibits sufficient rectification efficiency even for very short pulses. Although the rectification efficiency decreases with shorter pulsewidths, the efficiency can be further improved by optimizing the pulse repetition interval and input power.

articleTitle: Microwave-induced Plasma and its Microwave Rectification Effect
abstract: A 2450-MHz microwave-induced lamp based on an open-ended dielectric waveguide which directly transfer high-frequency power to the neon plasma without the needs of electrodes and wires is proposed. This device is a simple structure with low-power requirement and high controllability. It can excite a neon bulb at room temperature with 3 Watts microwave power. The minimum sustaining power for plasma is as low as 0.3 Watts. Two Dumet wires are inserted into the plasma and are connected to a resistor. It demonstrates that the microwave induced plasma can rectify microwaves into dc. The rectification efficiency reaches a maximum of 0.05% with the 1000 Ohm resistor and 1.88 W input power. Although the rectification efficiency is relatively low. However, it is a novel method for microwave rectification and possess a great potential in microwave power transfer applications.

articleTitle: Low Ripple Envelope Detection for Load Modulated Communication in SWIPT

authors.preferredName: Susanna Vital de Campos de Freitas

abstract: In this work we propose a new design methodology for envelope detectors in amplitude shift keyed communication. The method's premise is that a deliberately designed distortion can significantly improve the performance of a data receiver by reducing the bit error rate (BER). The main significance is in simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) applications where this envelope detector can be used to improve the recovery of messages transmitted from battery-less units employing load modulation. The key principle is the reduction of ripple voltage, which allows a battery-less unit to use a smaller modulation depth and thus remain in an impedance matched condition while receiving power and transmitting data simultaneously. A design criterion was developed to enable this improvement and implemented in a software-defined receiver (SDR). Data was transmitted through a wireless power transfer system designed for Qi purposes and recovered using the SDR, from which BER plots were produced and it was shown that the design indeed maximizes the performance.

articleTitle: Resistance and Q-factor calculation of single and double layer coils with split circular pattern
abstract: In the paper, resistance and quality factor (Q-factor) of single and double layer coils with split circular pattern are calculated according to frequency range from 125 kHz to 6.78 MHz to design an effective coil in magnetic coupling wireless power transfer. For calculation, method of volume filament model (VFM) is adopted. It is shown that coils of a split double layer circular pattern have lower resistance and higher Q-factor than those of a split single layer. For comparison, total metal thickness for single and double layer is the same. With higher frequency in the megahertz frequency range, Q-factors for the double layer coils are higher than those for the single layer. Also, Q-factor difference between single and double layer coils increases. Also, when total metal of the coils becomes thicker, resistance is reduced and Q-factor is improved. Additionally, the differences of resistance and Q-factor between single and double layer are reduced with thicker metal. For verification, several single and double layer coils of a split circular pattern with 0.5 oz, 1 oz, and 2 oz metal thick are fabricated. The calculation results are verified with the measurement and simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of Rectifier Circuit for Wireless Power Transfer to Pipeline Inspection Robots
abstract: Inspecting the safety of gas pipelines is essential for our lives. Recently, a novel method of pipeline inspection from inside by robots has been proposed and put to practical use. The robots can run a limited distance depending on their batteries, and the battery life is not long enough for the whole inspections. One of the methods to solve this problem is microwave wireless power transfer(MWPT). MWPT can make the distance longer because the approach eliminates the need of the batteries. We are focusing on the WPT with microwaves and rectifiers used in the receiving units of the new inspecting system. Their rectifiers should be small enough for installing to the inspecting robots. The limitation is a trapezoid, whose upper sides is 1.9 cm, lower side is 5.0 cm, and height is 5.0 cm. We designed a 2.45 GHz single-shunt rectifier with the former condition. The experimental results showed the maximum rf-dc conversion efficiency of 80.6%.

articleTitle: Harmonic Reflection Detection from 915-MHz SDR- Based RF Energy Harvesting Prototype System
abstract: In this paper the reflection detection of second harmonic from a 915-MHz radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting prototype system is demonstrated. The prototype system contains an RF power emitter and a power receiver. The power receiver is composed of a rectenna and a commercial power management demoboard. The power emitter includes two commercial software-defined radio (SDR) transceivers to act as a RF power radiator and a harmonic detector for energy harvesting and harmonic reflection detection, respectively. From the experimental results, the transmission power of about +18 dBm are delivered to the rectenna to start up the power management demo board to hunting electrical energy at a distance of 50 cm. By directly reading the measured harmonic power strength with a SDR tool, a detectable harmonic power level difference can be observed. The difference over 10 dB can be obtained. Thus, it can be used as an index signal to identify the directional position of the power receiver.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis for the Lossless Dielectric Material in Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: In this paper, we propose the analysis of dielectric sensitivity of transmitting and receiving coils in wireless power transmission system. The diameter of the dielectric disk under test is defined using the diameter of the coil, the transmission distance and the distribution of the electromagnetic field along the virtual vertical axis. The proposed method for acquiring the dielectric sensitivity is applied to two representative coil models and the validation of this analysis is proved by the simulated results.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit and coil design for spatial freedom of wireless charging
abstract: Wireless charging is widely used as a convenience that allows users to charge electronic devices without wires. However, the receiver on the wireless charging pad is not charged if the receiver is misaligned. Therefore, it is needed to adjust the center of the receiver well. This misalignment may greatly reduce the convenience of wireless charging. To overcome this limitation of wireless charging, a coil with an increased outer diameter and a double coil were designed to improve the positional freedom of receiver. The complex circuit of a double coil is converted into the T-equivalent circuit. The efficiency is obtained by measuring and simulating the Z-parameter at the frequency of 100 kHz. The efficiency of the coil with a large outer diameter and the double coil decreased at the center, but the efficiency improved when shifted by 15 mm. The trends in measurement and simulation are observed to be similar.

articleTitle: Evaluations of Induced Current in Human Cells and Enhancement of the Incubator’s Performance for Radio Wave Safety Experiments
abstract: We focused on the induced current generated from electromagnetic waves, which are exposed to human bodies. We have been developing an incubator that exposes 85 kHz magnetic field to objects and the induced current distribution on culture solutions are theoretically and numerically obtained. As a result, the induced current distribution is concentrated on a part of the exposed area. After confirming that the magnitude of the average induced current is appropriate, the concentration which disturbs the correct experiments is eliminated by using a Helmholtz coil structure. In conclusion, we revealed the estimation method of the induced current in human cells.

articleTitle: Inductive Resonant Coils for Biomedical Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: This study analyzes wireless transmission efficiency in magnetic resonance topology. In wireless power transmission systems, the overall efficiency is limited by the power consumption of coils. To improve the efficiency of wireless power transmission systems, this study proposes a suitable design for implantable devices by studying the shapes of coils, the distance between them, and the transmission media. Results show that efficiency declines as the distance between coils increases. Good efficiency is achieved under long-distance transmission when coils with large radii are used in transmitters. At short distances, small coils achieve better efficiency than large coils. The measurement results under an emulated human body experiment show that skin thickness is the key factor in transmission efficiency. The transmission efficiency under a pig skin thickness of 9 mm is 0.799% lower than that under the air medium.

articleTitle: Optimization of implant-type wireless rechargeable battery
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are served as a power source for various biomedical devices. Compared to the conventional LIBs, which are used in portable electric devices and electric vehicles, the implantable LIBs are required high safety and stable performance. In detail, the implantable LIBs should have high energy density due to limited space in the human body. Therefore, there has been a need for implantable LIBs having high energy density and long lifespan. In this study, the implantable LIB is designed by optimization of electrode composition in consideration of the energy density and cha rging/discharging performance. The designed implantable LIB has 30 mm × 9 mm × 3 mm (Length x width x thickness), sho wed high performance with 52 mAh of capacitance, and 166.4 mWh of power.

articleTitle: Beamforming with Beam-Steered Pilots in a Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: In an RF wireless power transfer system, transmit beamforming can improve energy transmission efficiency by concentrating radiated energy toward a receiving device. For optimal transmit beamforming, it is necessary for the energy transmitter to know the exact direction of the receiving device. In this paper, we propose a wireless power transfer system based on beam-steered pilot signals. In the proposed system, the receiver estimates its own direction relative to the transmitter using the beam-steered pilot signals and feeds the estimate back to the transmitter. Then, the transmitter emits beamformed energy signals to the corresponding direction. We evaluate the effect of the resolution of beam-steered pilot signals on the performance of the direction estimation scheme and analyze the efficiency of wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Design for MW-Level Microwave Power Transmission in SSPS Demonstration
abstract: According to the space solar power satellite development strategies in China, a mega-watt (MW)-level SSPS on geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) demonstration will be carried out after 2030. Microwave power beam steering must be considered for the demonstration. Beam steering methods are reviewed for microwave power transmission applications. Then beam steering requirements are investigated for MW-level SSPS demonstration. Beam steering technology is proposed for the demonstration with consideration of MW-level microwave power transmitting subsystem design.

articleTitle: A 5.8 GHz Reconfigurable in-Phase Power Divider for Microwave Power Transmission
abstract: In this paper, a 5.8 GHz reconfigurable in-phase power divider is presented. A new equivalent circuit of the tunable transmission line with varactor diodes is introduced to apply the concept of proposed divider by P.-L. Chi et al. to the design of 5.8 GHz reconfigurable power divider. In the simulation, the validity of the proposed divider is confirmed and the adverse effect of parasitic resistance of varactor diodes on the divider's performance is analyzed. The simulated results show, in the range of 0 - 15 dB dividing ratio, the designed divider operate with the output phase difference of less than 0.15 deg. and the insertion loss of less than 1.76 dB.

articleTitle: Chipless Strain Sensor using Phase Modulation
abstract: Even though Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) is nowadays widely applied, there is one issue that keeps preventing its massive adoption: its tag's cost, which is dependant on the cost of its Integrated Circuit (IC). To overcome this difficulty, efforts have been made to develop new chipless RFID tags with identifying and also sensing capabilities. Thus, this paper proposes a chipless RFID tag capable of performing strain sensing. The paper presents several aspects related to the sensor development, such as: material characterization and phase modulations; and presents its results by means of reflected power measurements.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimal Transmitting Source for Midfield Wireless Powering of Micro-implant
abstract: Midfield wireless power transfer has been proven as a solution for biomedical micro-implant that can operate at nearly any location in the body. Some previous experiments using an external patterned structure as optimal source demonstrated magnetic and current density focusing characteristic on multilayers tissue, therefore, significantly enhancing efficiency for wireless powering to miniature receivers than conventional inductively coupled coils. This paper proposed a novel compact and simple source transmitter while conserving convergence effect on human tissue.

articleTitle: Signal Detection Method Based on Peak to Average Ratio for Frequency Shift Multitone SWIPT System
abstract: Battery-less devices that operate on wireless power transfer have a relatively small operating area due to the limited transmit power from the source. Multitone based waveforms are considered to be one of the techniques to expand this operating range. However, they require some bandwidth to achieve this feature. By sharing the bandwidth required for multitone waveforms and superimposing information on the power, it is possible to transmit both power and information at the same time, which is known as simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). In this paper, we introduce a method of detecting signal by measuring peak to average power ratio (PAPR) in order to reduce the computational cost for frequency shift keying type SWIPT instead of observing frequency-domain signals by using fast Fourier transforms. Signal decoding is possible by seeing the PAPR difference as the frequencies of intermodulation signals varies with difference tone arrangement. We demonstrate this through circuit simulation with Advanced Design Systems (ADS) and show how many bits could encode for tones of 3 and 4. In addition, we categories which tone variations in the frequency domain would lead to obtaining a specific PAPR at the receiver end.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer

articleTitle: RBF Modeling for Magnetic MIMO WPT: Detection, Estimation and Prediction
abstract: Magnetic MIMO is a new paradigm for near field and high efficiency wireless power transfer (WPT) system, and mutual inductive among coils is an essential factor to determine the power transfer efficiency which is difficult to attain in a mobile scenario. In this letter, we propose a neural network method using radial based function (RBF) to model the wireless power propagation of magnetic resonance MIMO. We use this model to detect the receiver and predict the received voltage. Experimental results indicate that the RBF model is highly accurate and it is an efficient tool for magnetic channel estimation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetic Energy Harvester for Inspection Robot of Power Line Using Saturable Inductor
abstract: Recently, magnetic energy harvesting is a promising technologies for self-sustainable operation of devices around power line. However, the magnetic energy harvester has a problem that magnetic core material is saturated at high current condition. In this paper, we analyzed the power harvesting by considering magnetic saturation in magnetic material. Using B-H curve, we analyzed magnetizing inductance according to varying primary current. This analysis makes it possible to predict harvested power in saturated condition, which the conventional method cannot predict. To confirm the validity of this paper, magnetic core materials were fabricated and measured by B-H curve tracer. The experiments were prevailed from 5A to 250A primary current.

articleTitle: Class E Asymmetric Inverter Implementation for Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: The paper investigates the implementation of the phase-controlled Class E asymmetric inverter topology in a near-field wireless power transfer application. The purpose of this design is to achieve high efficiency performance and desired output power through duty cycle and phase shift compensation under coupling and load variations, which is an issue caused by unintentional misalignment of transformer coils. Since the application is near-field, the coupling coefficient k ranging from 0.4 to 0.6 was utilized through simulations, and the appropriate compensation was applied to improve the overall power efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Design of a reflective metasurface with a transmit lens using near-field beam focusing
abstract: In this paper, a design of a reflective metasurface with a transmit lens is proposed to mechanically adjust a focal point of wireless power transmission using near-field beam focusing. The metasurface with 10 by 10 unit cells is modeled to provide an incident semi-planewave toward the transmission lens. The transmit lens can then focus the electric field at the focal point to increase the WPT efficiency, and the location of the lens can be mechanically adjusted to easily change the beam focusing point. The resulting electric field intensities are 26.4 dBV/m, 23.8 dBV/m, and 23.4 dBV/m at focusing points of 140 mm, 235.8 mm, and 342 mm, respectively, when the transmit lens is located at heights of 50 mm, 100 mm, and 150 mm along the bore-sight direction.
